Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a large, well-circumscribed, radiolucent (fat-density) mass in the right cardiophrenic angle that obscures the right heart border but spares the lung parenchyma, which is characteristic of a giant thymolipoma. Other options like collapse, effusion, or pneumothorax would present with opacity, fluid levels, or absent lung markings respectively, none of which match this fatty appearance.
